# VisionAssist

> VisionAssist is an open-source, offline-first assistive vision system that speaks Hindi, built for blind and visually impaired users. It runs on a laptop with a webcam: YOLOv8 object detection with spoken Hindi alerts (what, how close, which side), OCR for reading signs and labels, scene description through a vision-language model, and offline Hindi voice commands (Vosk). Hindi speech uses an offline Piper voice. It is an assistive aid, not a safety device.

Key facts:
- Language: Hindi (Devanagari) for everything the user hears or reads; Hinglish on screen.
- Offline: object alerts, Hindi speech, voice commands and "what changed" work without internet. OCR and scene description use free online APIs by default; `LOCAL_ONLY=true` keeps all frames on the device.
- Stack: Python 3.10 to 3.12, YOLOv8n, Piper TTS, Vosk, OpenCV, Flask, Tesseract, OpenRouter, OCR.space.
- License: MIT.
- Evaluation: 80 synthetic scenarios; results show pipeline behaviour, not real-world accuracy.
